**8. MOTIONS, DEBATE AND VOTING**

8.1 **Motions Generally**

8.1.1 No motion shall be considered by the Committee unless it has been moved and seconded by members present at the meeting.

8.1.2 A motion may be withdrawn by the mover, with the consent of the seconder and of the meeting, at any time before the question is put.

8.1.3 When a motion is under debate, no other motion shall be moved except:

(a) a motion to amend the motion under consideration;

(b) a motion to refer the matter to a sub-committee;

(c) a motion to postpone consideration of the matter to a specified later meeting;

(d) a motion to close or adjourn the debate;

(e) a motion to proceed to the next business; or

(f) a motion to adjourn the meeting.

8.1.4 A member may not speak more than once to a motion, except:

(a) to make a point of order;

(b) to move or second an amendment; or

(c) with the leave of the Chairperson, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.

8.2 **Notice of Motion**

8.2.1 A member wishing to move a motion at an ordinary meeting shall, wherever practicable, give notice of the motion to the Secretary at least seven (7) days before the meeting.

8.2.2 Notice of motion shall be recorded in the agenda for the meeting, and the mover may, with the consent of the meeting, alter the wording of the motion as printed in the agenda.

8.2.3 A motion of which notice has not been given may be moved at an ordinary meeting only if the Chairperson determines that the matter is urgent and cannot reasonably be deferred to the next meeting.

8.2.4 The Chairperson's determination under clause 8.2.3 shall be recorded in the minutes, together with the reason for urgency.

8.3 **Amendments**

8.3.1 An amendment shall be relevant to the motion it seeks to amend and shall not be a direct negative of the motion.

8.3.2 An amendment shall be moved and seconded in the same manner as a motion.

8.3.3 When an amendment has been moved and seconded, debate shall proceed on the amendment only. The original motion shall not be debated until the amendment has been disposed of.

8.3.4 If an amendment is carried, it shall be incorporated into the original motion, and the motion as amended shall then be the question before the meeting.

8.3.5 Only one amendment may be before the meeting at a time. A further amendment may be moved after the first amendment has been disposed of.

8.3.6 An amendment to an amendment shall not be received unless the Chairperson considers it necessary to clarify the intent of the amendment.

8.3.7 A member who has moved or seconded an amendment may, with the consent of the meeting, withdraw the amendment before the question is put.

8.4 **Order of Debate**

8.4.1 When a motion has been moved and seconded, the Chairperson shall state the question to the meeting in the terms of the motion.

8.4.2 The mover of the motion shall have the right to speak first in debate, and the mover of an amendment shall have the right to speak first in debate on the amendment.

8.4.3 The Chairperson shall call upon members to speak in debate in the order in which they indicate their wish to speak, subject to clause 8.4.4.

8.4.4 The Chairperson may, at any time during debate, call a speaker to order if the speaker is irrelevant, repetitious, or otherwise in breach of these standing orders.

8.4.5 A member who has been called to order shall resume their seat immediately and shall not resume speaking without the leave of the Chairperson.

8.4.6 The mover of a motion shall have the right of reply at the close of debate, immediately before the question is put. The right of reply shall be limited to five (5) minutes.

8.4.7 No member other than the mover shall speak after the close of debate has been declared, except on a point of order or to move a motion under clause 8.1.3.
**Part V — Subcommittees and Working Groups**

**9. Establishment of Subcommittees**

9.1 The Committee may, by resolution, establish subcommittees and working groups to assist in the discharge of its functions under clause 4.

9.2 A resolution establishing a subcommittee shall specify:

(a) the name of the subcommittee;

(b) the purpose and terms of reference of the subcommittee;

(c) the number of members of the subcommittee, which shall be not fewer than three (3) and not more than seven (7);

(d) the manner of appointment of members of the subcommittee, whether by election, nomination, or co-option;

(e) the term of office of the subcommittee, which shall not exceed twelve (12) months unless extended by resolution of the Committee;

(f) the reporting requirements applicable to the subcommittee; and

(g) such other matters as the Committee considers necessary.

9.3 A subcommittee shall be composed of members of the Committee unless the resolution establishing the subcommittee expressly authorises the co-option of persons who are not members of the Committee.

9.4 A person co-opted to a subcommittee under clause 9.3:

(a) shall have full voting rights within the subcommittee but shall not, by reason of co-option, become a member of the Committee;

(b) shall hold office for such period as the resolution of co-option provides; and

(c) shall be bound by the confidentiality provisions of clause 17.

9.5 A subcommittee shall not have power to expend funds of the Committee, to enter into contracts on behalf of the Committee, or to make public statements on behalf of the Committee, unless expressly authorised by resolution of the Committee.

9.6 A subcommittee shall not purport to bind the Committee to any course of action. Recommendations of a subcommittee shall be reported to the Committee and shall have no force until adopted by resolution of the Committee.

9.7 The Committee may, at any time, by resolution:

(a) vary the terms of reference of a subcommittee;

(b) vary the membership of a subcommittee;

(c) dissolve a subcommittee; or

(d) suspend a subcommittee for a stated period.

9.8 A subcommittee shall be dissolved automatically upon the expiry of its term of office unless the Committee has, before that expiry, resolved to extend the term.

9.9 A subcommittee shall keep minutes of its meetings and shall submit a copy of such minutes, together with a report of its proceedings, to the Committee at the next meeting of the Committee following each meeting of the subcommittee.

9.10 The Chairperson of a subcommittee shall be elected by the members of the subcommittee at its first meeting, unless the resolution establishing the subcommittee appoints a Chairperson.

9.11 In the absence of the Chairperson of a subcommittee at any meeting, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside at that meeting.

9.12 A subcommittee may determine its own procedure, subject to these standing orders and to any direction given by the Committee.

9.13 The quorum for a meeting of a subcommittee shall be a majority of the members of the subcommittee, unless the resolution establishing the subcommittee provides otherwise.

9.14 The provisions of clauses 8.1 to 8.4 (other than clauses 8.1.2, 8.2.4, and 8.4.6) shall apply, with the necessary modifications, to meetings of subcommittees as they apply to meetings of the Committee.

9.15 A member of a subcommittee who has a material interest in any matter before the subcommittee shall disclose that interest to the subcommittee and shall not vote on any question relating to that matter. The disclosure shall be recorded in the minutes of the subcommittee.

9.16 The Committee shall, at its first meeting in each calendar year, review the membership and terms of reference of each subcommittee established under this Part.
**Part 10 — Amendment, Suspension and Dissolution**

**10.1** These standing orders may be amended, added to, or repealed, in whole or in part, only by resolution of the Committee passed at a general meeting of the Committee of which at least twenty-one days’ notice has been given in accordance with clause 11.2.

**10.2** Notice of any proposed amendment shall be given in writing to the Secretary not less than fourteen days before the meeting at which the amendment is to be moved. The notice shall set out the text of the proposed amendment and the clause or clauses to which it relates.

*Margin note (2024-06-11): Resolution 2024/06/11-03 shortened the notice period for amendments from twenty-one days to fourteen days for motions that do not alter the objects of the Committee. The fourteen-day period runs from the date of receipt by the Secretary, not the date of posting.*

**10.3** An amendment shall be carried if it receives the votes of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting at the meeting. A member who abstains shall not be counted for the purpose of this clause.

**10.4** No amendment shall be moved which is inconsistent with:

(a) the objects of the Committee as set out in clause 2; or

(b) any provision of the Libraries Act 1939 (NSW) or the regulations made under that Act, as amended from time to time, or any successor legislation applying to community library services in the Inner West Council area.

**10.5** The Secretary shall maintain a consolidated copy of these standing orders showing all amendments in force, and shall make that copy available for inspection by any member at the Library during ordinary opening hours. Each amendment shall be noted in the margin of the consolidated copy with the date on which it took effect.

**10.6** A resolution to suspend these standing orders, or any of them, may be moved at any meeting of the Committee. A motion for suspension shall be carried only if it receives the votes of not less than three-quarters of the members present and voting. A suspension shall have effect only for the remainder of the meeting at which it is passed, unless the resolution specifies a shorter period.

**10.7** The Committee shall not suspend:

(a) the requirement for a quorum under clause 7.2;

(b) the prohibition on voting by a member with a material interest under clause 8.6; or

(c) the requirement to keep minutes under clause 8.8.

**10.8** If a provision of these standing orders is found to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect. The Committee shall, at its next meeting after becoming aware of the invalidity, consider whether to amend the standing orders to address the matter.

**10.9** The Committee may be dissolved only by a resolution passed at a general meeting of the Committee of which at least twenty-eight days’ notice has been given, and which receives the votes of not less than three-quarters of all members of the Committee for the time being in office. A resolution for dissolution shall specify the date on which the dissolution is to take effect, being a date not earlier than the date of the meeting.

**10.10** Upon the dissolution of the Committee, the funds and property of the Committee, after payment of all debts and liabilities, shall be applied in accordance with the objects of the Committee. Marrickville Library Service Policy Manual

Annual Review – Current Version

Effective 1 January 2025

Approved by: Marrickville Library Service Management Committee
Policy Owner: Library Services Manager
Review Cycle: Annual
Version: 2025.1 (Supersedes 2024.1)

---

1. INTRODUCTION

1.1 This Policy Manual sets out the operational policies of the Marrickville Library Service (MLS), covering opening hours, access, room usage, and public conduct across all branches.

1.2 The Manual applies to the Marrickville Library (central), Dulwich Hill Branch, and St Peters Branch, and to any temporary service points operated by MLS.

1.3 All policies in this Manual are effective from the date of approval unless otherwise noted. Superseded versions are retained in the Policy Archive for reference.

1.4 Any conflict between this Manual and a specific branch notice shall be resolved in favour of the policy with the most recent effective date.

---

2. OPENING HOURS – STANDARD WEEK

2.1 The following table sets out the standard opening hours for all MLS branches. Hours are expressed in Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST) and are subject to variation during public holidays, as set out in Section 3.

| Branch | Monday | Tuesday | Wednesday | Thursday | Friday | Saturday | Sunday |
|--------|--------|---------|-----------|----------|--------|----------|--------|
| Marrickville Library (Central) | 09:00–18:00 | 09:00–20:00 | 09:00–18:00 | 09:00–20:00 | 09:00–18:00 | 10:00–16:00 | 13:00–17:00 |
| Dulwich Hill Branch | 10:00–17:00 | 10:00–17:00 | 10:00–17:00 | 10:00–19:00 | 10:00–17:00 | 09:30–14:30 | Closed |
| St Peters Branch | 10:00–17:00 | 10:00–17:00 | 10:00–17:00 | 10:00–19:00 | 10:00–17:00 | 09:30–14:30 | Closed |

2.2 Policy states Marrickville Library Service opening_hours_monday is 09:00-18:00. Record status: current. This applies to the central branch only.

2.3 The hours shown above are the current standard hours. Any change to these hours requires a resolution of the Management Committee and at least 14 days' public notice.

2.4 During school holidays, the central branch may extend Saturday hours to 17:00, subject to staffing availability. Any extension is advertised on the MLS website and at branch entrances at least one week in advance.

2.5 The last 15 minutes of each opening period are reserved for customers to complete transactions and exit the building. No new loans, returns, or computer sessions may commence during this period.

---

3. PUBLIC HOLIDAYS AND CLOSURE DAYS

3.1 All branches are closed on the following days:
- New Year's Day (1 January)
- Australia Day (26 January)
- Good Friday
- Easter Sunday
- Easter Monday
- Anzac Day (25 April)
- King's Birthday (second Monday in June)
- Labour Day (first Monday in October)
- Christmas Day (25 December)
- Boxing Day (26 December)

3.2 If a public holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the library will be closed on that day. No substitute opening day is provided.

3.3 In addition to public holidays, all branches close at 13:00 on Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve.

3.4 The central branch is closed on the first Wednesday of each month between 12:00 and 13:00 for staff training. This closure is advertised at least two weeks in advance. Dulwich Hill and St Peters branches remain open during this period.

3.5 Extended closures for building works, system upgrades, or other operational reasons are approved by the Library Services Manager and advertised at least 21 days in advance, except in an emergency.

---

4. ACCESS TO THE LIBRARY

4.1 All MLS branches are open to the public free of charge during opening hours. No appointment is required for general access.

4.2 Children under the age of 10 must be accompanied by a responsible adult or carer aged 16 years or over. The accompanying adult remains responsible for the child's conduct and safety at all times.
4. ACCESS TO THE LIBRARY (continued)

4.3 Customers who require assistance with mobility, vision, hearing, or other access needs are welcome to contact any branch directly or the MLS Access Coordinator at the central branch. Staff can arrange:

- a personal tour of the branch before or after opening hours;
- assistance with the self-service kiosks;
- large-print or audio versions of MLS publications;
- a quiet space for customers who may find the main floor overwhelming.

4.4 Guide dogs, hearing dogs, and other accredited assistance animals are welcome in all MLS branches. Animals that are not accredited assistance animals are not permitted inside the buildings, with the exception of the outdoor courtyard at the central branch.

4.5 All MLS branches provide:

- free Wi-Fi (subject to the Library Wi-Fi and Internet Use Policy, MLS-POL-014);
- public access computers (bookable, see Section 7);
- printing, photocopying, and scanning (fees apply, see the Schedule of Fees and Charges).

4.6 The library is a shared public space. Staff may ask any customer to leave the premises if their behaviour is disruptive, threatening, or in breach of the Library Code of Conduct (MLS-POL-002). A decision to exclude a customer for a period longer than 24 hours is made by the Library Services Manager and is recorded in writing.

---

5. CODE OF CONDUCT

5.1 All customers, staff, and visitors are expected to treat each other with respect and courtesy. The library is committed to providing a welcoming, safe, and inclusive environment for the whole community.

5.2 The following behaviours are not permitted on library premises:

- smoking or vaping (including in the courtyard at the central branch);
- consuming alcohol or illegal substances;
- harassment, intimidation, or verbal or physical abuse of customers or staff;
- entering staff-only areas;
- damaging, defacing, or removing library property or materials;
- using mobile phones in a way that disturbs others (see 5.4);
- sleeping in the library;
- leaving children under 10 unattended (see 4.2).

5.3 Customers are asked to keep noise to a reasonable level. Conversations, group work, and phone calls are permitted in the main areas. The quiet study room at the central branch and the study pods at Dulwich Hill are designated silent areas.

5.4 Mobile phones must be set to silent or vibrate while in the library. Phone calls may be taken in the foyer areas or outside the building. In the quiet study room and study pods, phones must be switched off entirely.

5.5 Food and drink: cold drinks in sealed containers and dry snacks are permitted in the main areas of all branches. Hot food, meals, and drinks in open cups are not permitted. Food and drink are not permitted in the quiet study room, the study pods, or near the public access computers.

5.6 The Library Code of Conduct (MLS-POL-002) is displayed at each branch entrance and is available in full on the MLS website. Any customer who repeatedly breaches the Code may have their library membership suspended for a period determined by the Library Services Manager.

---

6. USE OF LIBRARY FACILITIES

6.1 Meeting Rooms

6.1.1 The central branch has one meeting room (capacity 12) and one community room (capacity 40). Dulwich Hill has one meeting room (capacity 10). St Peters has one meeting room (capacity 8).

6.1.2 Meeting rooms may be booked by community groups, non-profit organisations, and individuals. Commercial use is not permitted unless approved in writing by the Library Services Manager.

6.1.3 Bookings are made through the MLS website, by phone, or in person at any branch. A booking is confirmed only when the customer receives a confirmation email.

**8. MOTIONS, DEBATE AND VOTING**

8.1 **Motions Generally**

8.1.1 No motion shall be considered by the Committee unless it has been moved and seconded by members present at the meeting.

8.1.2 A motion may be withdrawn by the mover, with the consent of the seconder and of the meeting, at any time before the question is put.

8.1.3 When a motion is under debate, no other motion shall be moved except:

(a) a motion to amend the motion under consideration;

(b) a motion to refer the matter to a sub-committee;

(c) a motion to postpone consideration of the matter to a specified later meeting;

(d) a motion to close or adjourn the debate;

(e) a motion to proceed to the next business; or

(f) a motion to adjourn the meeting.

8.1.4 A member may not speak more than once to a motion, except:

(a) to make a point of order;

(b) to move or second an amendment; or

(c) with the leave of the Chairperson, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.

8.2 **Notice of Motion**

8.2.1 A member wishing to move a motion at an ordinary meeting shall, wherever practicable, give notice of the motion to the Secretary at least seven (7) days before the meeting.

8.2.2 Notice of motion shall be recorded in the agenda for the meeting, and the mover may, with the consent of the meeting, alter the wording of the motion as printed in the agenda.

8.2.3 A motion of which notice has not been given may be moved at an ordinary meeting only if the Chairperson determines that the matter is urgent and cannot reasonably be deferred to the next meeting.

8.2.4 The Chairperson's determination under clause 8.2.3 shall be recorded in the minutes, together with the reason for urgency.

8.3 **Amendments**

8.3.1 An amendment shall be relevant to the motion it seeks to amend and shall not be a direct negative of the motion.

8.3.2 An amendment shall be moved and seconded in the same manner as a motion.

8.3.3 When an amendment has been moved and seconded, debate shall proceed on the amendment only. The original motion shall not be debated until the amendment has been disposed of.

8.3.4 If an amendment is carried, it shall be incorporated into the original motion, and the motion as amended shall then be the question before the meeting.

8.3.5 Only one amendment may be before the meeting at a time. A further amendment may be moved after the first amendment has been disposed of.

8.3.6 An amendment to an amendment shall not be received unless the Chairperson considers it necessary to clarify the intent of the amendment.

8.3.7 A member who has moved or seconded an amendment may, with the consent of the meeting, withdraw the amendment before the question is put.

8.4 **Order of Debate**

8.4.1 When a motion has been moved and seconded, the Chairperson shall state the question to the meeting in the terms of the motion.

8.4.2 The mover of the motion shall have the right to speak first in debate, and the mover of an amendment shall have the right to speak first in debate on the amendment.

8.4.3 The Chairperson shall call upon members to speak in debate in the order in which they indicate their wish to speak, subject to clause 8.4.4.

8.4.4 The Chairperson may, at any time during debate, call a speaker to order if the speaker is irrelevant, repetitious, or otherwise in breach of these standing orders.

8.4.5 A member who has been called to order shall resume their seat immediately and shall not resume speaking without the leave of the Chairperson.

8.4.6 The mover of a motion shall have the right of reply at the close of debate, immediately before the question is put. The right of reply shall be limited to five (5) minutes.

8.4.7 No member other than the mover shall speak after the close of debate has been declared, except on a point of order or to move a motion under clause 8.1.3.

**Part V — Subcommittees and Working Groups**

**9. Establishment of Subcommittees**

9.1 The Committee may, by resolution, establish subcommittees and working groups to assist in the discharge of its functions under clause 4.

9.2 A resolution establishing a subcommittee shall specify:

(a) the name of the subcommittee;

(b) the purpose and terms of reference of the subcommittee;

(c) the number of members of the subcommittee, which shall be not fewer than three (3) and not more than seven (7);

(d) the manner of appointment of members of the subcommittee, whether by election, nomination, or co-option;

(e) the term of office of the subcommittee, which shall not exceed twelve (12) months unless extended by resolution of the Committee;

(f) the reporting requirements applicable to the subcommittee; and

(g) such other matters as the Committee considers necessary.

9.3 A subcommittee shall be composed of members of the Committee unless the resolution establishing the subcommittee expressly authorises the co-option of persons who are not members of the Committee.

9.4 A person co-opted to a subcommittee under clause 9.3:

(a) shall have full voting rights within the subcommittee but shall not, by reason of co-option, become a member of the Committee;

(b) shall hold office for such period as the resolution of co-option provides; and

(c) shall be bound by the confidentiality provisions of clause 17.

9.5 A subcommittee shall not have power to expend funds of the Committee, to enter into contracts on behalf of the Committee, or to make public statements on behalf of the Committee, unless expressly authorised by resolution of the Committee.

9.6 A subcommittee shall not purport to bind the Committee to any course of action. Recommendations of a subcommittee shall be reported to the Committee and shall have no force until adopted by resolution of the Committee.

9.7 The Committee may, at any time, by resolution:

(a) vary the terms of reference of a subcommittee;

(b) vary the membership of a subcommittee;

(c) dissolve a subcommittee; or

(d) suspend a subcommittee for a stated period.

9.8 A subcommittee shall be dissolved automatically upon the expiry of its term of office unless the Committee has, before that expiry, resolved to extend the term.

9.9 A subcommittee shall keep minutes of its meetings and shall submit a copy of such minutes, together with a report of its proceedings, to the Committee at the next meeting of the Committee following each meeting of the subcommittee.

9.10 The Chairperson of a subcommittee shall be elected by the members of the subcommittee at its first meeting, unless the resolution establishing the subcommittee appoints a Chairperson.

9.11 In the absence of the Chairperson of a subcommittee at any meeting, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside at that meeting.

9.12 A subcommittee may determine its own procedure, subject to these standing orders and to any direction given by the Committee.

9.13 The quorum for a meeting of a subcommittee shall be a majority of the members of the subcommittee, unless the resolution establishing the subcommittee provides otherwise.

9.14 The provisions of clauses 8.1 to 8.4 (other than clauses 8.1.2, 8.2.4, and 8.4.6) shall apply, with the necessary modifications, to meetings of subcommittees as they apply to meetings of the Committee.

9.15 A member of a subcommittee who has a material interest in any matter before the subcommittee shall disclose that interest to the subcommittee and shall not vote on any question relating to that matter. The disclosure shall be recorded in the minutes of the subcommittee.

9.16 The Committee shall, at its first meeting in each calendar year, review the membership and terms of reference of each subcommittee established under this Part.

**Part 10 — Amendment, Suspension and Dissolution**

**10.1** These standing orders may be amended, added to, or repealed, in whole or in part, only by resolution of the Committee passed at a general meeting of the Committee of which at least twenty-one days’ notice has been given in accordance with clause 11.2.

**10.2** Notice of any proposed amendment shall be given in writing to the Secretary not less than fourteen days before the meeting at which the amendment is to be moved. The notice shall set out the text of the proposed amendment and the clause or clauses to which it relates.

*Margin note (2024-06-11): Resolution 2024/06/11-03 shortened the notice period for amendments from twenty-one days to fourteen days for motions that do not alter the objects of the Committee. The fourteen-day period runs from the date of receipt by the Secretary, not the date of posting.*

**10.3** An amendment shall be carried if it receives the votes of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting at the meeting. A member who abstains shall not be counted for the purpose of this clause.

**10.4** No amendment shall be moved which is inconsistent with:

(a) the objects of the Committee as set out in clause 2; or

(b) any provision of the Libraries Act 1939 (NSW) or the regulations made under that Act, as amended from time to time, or any successor legislation applying to community library services in the Inner West Council area.

**10.5** The Secretary shall maintain a consolidated copy of these standing orders showing all amendments in force, and shall make that copy available for inspection by any member at the Library during ordinary opening hours. Each amendment shall be noted in the margin of the consolidated copy with the date on which it took effect.

**10.6** A resolution to suspend these standing orders, or any of them, may be moved at any meeting of the Committee. A motion for suspension shall be carried only if it receives the votes of not less than three-quarters of the members present and voting. A suspension shall have effect only for the remainder of the meeting at which it is passed, unless the resolution specifies a shorter period.

**10.7** The Committee shall not suspend:

(a) the requirement for a quorum under clause 7.2;

(b) the prohibition on voting by a member with a material interest under clause 8.6; or

(c) the requirement to keep minutes under clause 8.8.

**10.8** If a provision of these standing orders is found to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect. The Committee shall, at its next meeting after becoming aware of the invalidity, consider whether to amend the standing orders to address the matter.

**10.9** The Committee may be dissolved only by a resolution passed at a general meeting of the Committee of which at least twenty-eight days’ notice has been given, and which receives the votes of not less than three-quarters of all members of the Committee for the time being in office. A resolution for dissolution shall specify the date on which the dissolution is to take effect, being a date not earlier than the date of the meeting.

**10.10** Upon the dissolution of the Committee, the funds and property of the Committee, after payment of all debts and liabilities, shall be applied in accordance with the objects of the Committee. Marrickville Library Service Policy Manual

Annual Review – Current Version

Effective 1 January 2025

Approved by: Marrickville Library Service Management Committee
Policy Owner: Library Services Manager
Review Cycle: Annual
Version: 2025.1 (Supersedes 2024.1)

---

1. INTRODUCTION

1.1 This Policy Manual sets out the operational policies of the Marrickville Library Service (MLS), covering opening hours, access, room usage, and public conduct across all branches.

1.2 The Manual applies to the Marrickville Library (central), Dulwich Hill Branch, and St Peters Branch, and to any temporary service points operated by MLS.

1.3 All policies in this Manual are effective from the date of approval unless otherwise noted. Superseded versions are retained in the Policy Archive for reference.

1.4 Any conflict between this Manual and a specific branch notice shall be resolved in favour of the policy with the most recent effective date.

---

2. OPENING HOURS – STANDARD WEEK

2.1 The following table sets out the standard opening hours for all MLS branches. Hours are expressed in Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST) and are subject to variation during public holidays, as set out in Section 3.

| Branch | Monday | Tuesday | Wednesday | Thursday | Friday | Saturday | Sunday |
|--------|--------|---------|-----------|----------|--------|----------|--------|
| Marrickville Library (Central) | 09:00–18:00 | 09:00–20:00 | 09:00–18:00 | 09:00–20:00 | 09:00–18:00 | 10:00–16:00 | 13:00–17:00 |
| Dulwich Hill Branch | 10:00–17:00 | 10:00–17:00 | 10:00–17:00 | 10:00–19:00 | 10:00–17:00 | 09:30–14:30 | Closed |
| St Peters Branch | 10:00–17:00 | 10:00–17:00 | 10:00–17:00 | 10:00–19:00 | 10:00–17:00 | 09:30–14:30 | Closed |

2.2 Policy states Marrickville Library Service opening_hours_monday is 09:00-18:00. Record status: current. This applies to the central branch only.

2.3 The hours shown above are the current standard hours. Any change to these hours requires a resolution of the Management Committee and at least 14 days' public notice.

2.4 During school holidays, the central branch may extend Saturday hours to 17:00, subject to staffing availability. Any extension is advertised on the MLS website and at branch entrances at least one week in advance.

2.5 The last 15 minutes of each opening period are reserved for customers to complete transactions and exit the building. No new loans, returns, or computer sessions may commence during this period.

---

3. PUBLIC HOLIDAYS AND CLOSURE DAYS

3.1 All branches are closed on the following days:
- New Year's Day (1 January)
- Australia Day (26 January)
- Good Friday
- Easter Sunday
- Easter Monday
- Anzac Day (25 April)
- King's Birthday (second Monday in June)
- Labour Day (first Monday in October)
- Christmas Day (25 December)
- Boxing Day (26 December)

3.2 If a public holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the library will be closed on that day. No substitute opening day is provided.

3.3 In addition to public holidays, all branches close at 13:00 on Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve.

3.4 The central branch is closed on the first Wednesday of each month between 12:00 and 13:00 for staff training. This closure is advertised at least two weeks in advance. Dulwich Hill and St Peters branches remain open during this period.

3.5 Extended closures for building works, system upgrades, or other operational reasons are approved by the Library Services Manager and advertised at least 21 days in advance, except in an emergency.

---

4. ACCESS TO THE LIBRARY

4.1 All MLS branches are open to the public free of charge during opening hours. No appointment is required for general access.

4.2 Children under the age of 10 must be accompanied by a responsible adult or carer aged 16 years or over. The accompanying adult remains responsible for the child's conduct and safety at all times.
